title: Dynamic runbook injection and PagerDuty context enrichment for traced incidents
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Problem: When high-severity incidents fire, responders spend time gathering context (top traces, correlated logs/metrics, relevant dashboards) and manually selecting runbooks. This increases MTTR and causes inconsistent postmortems. Goal: Implement a system that automatically enriches PagerDuty incidents and Slack alert threads with curated incident context (trace links, top correlated metrics/log snippets), and injects a suggested, editable runbook into the incident and Slack thread. Additionally seed a draft postmortem with an initial timeline generated from traces and critical logs to accelerate RCA.
acceptance_criteria: PagerDuty incidents created from severity>=P1 alerts include a pd_metadata payload with: primary_trace_link, top_3_error_spans, top_5_correlated_logs (links/snippets), and a suggested runbook ID
Slack alert messages posted to ops channels include ephemeral 'Open Runbook' CTA that expands to the suggested runbook content and editable checklist

On-call responders can accept the suggested runbook which creates a pinned runbook section in the PD incident and adds a draft postmortem doc pre-populated with timeline entries derived from trace spans
The enrichment flow respects data plane RBAC and redaction rules; sensitive fields are never forwarded to PD/Slack without KMS-enforced access
Automated tests validate that injected context links resolve to the correct tracing UI and that the top-3 correlated metrics match the alert's metric fingerprint
Feature rollout can be toggled per-service and per-environment via Console flags and does not affect services not opted-in
implementation_notes: Instrument the observability-events pipeline to emit an incident-context object when an alert crosses severity thresholds

Add a new enrichment service (obs-enricher) that subscribes to the pipeline, queries traces (by span id fingerprint), performs simple correlation over metrics and logs, and synthesizes a runbook suggestion using templates stored in Console
Enricher will attach a signed context blob to PD via Events API v2; for Slack use message buttons + ephemeral views for the runbook editor
Implement consent toggle and sensitive-data marker checks in the enrichment path; default to redacted snippets for non-admin channels
Create small library in ops-sdk for verifying signature and expanding context in PD/Slack integration codepaths
Seed postmortem doc via Confluence API using a template that includes sections: timeline (auto-filled), impact, root-cause hypotheses, immediate mitigation, and owner assignments
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): opt-in for infra services only; enable on 2 non-prod teams and observe false-positive enrichment for 2 weeks
Phase 2: expand to critical hosted services and Dedicated control plane; run a paid-beta with 3 customers for PD enrichment
Phase 3: GA toggle in Console, enable for all Redwood-managed alerts with an opt-out default for customer-managed alerts
Monitoring: add metrics for enrichment_latency_ms, enrichment_failures, runbook_accept_rate, postmortem_seed_success
Fallbacks: if enrichment service fails, send standard alert without enrichment and create a ticket in obs-enricher backlog
testing_plan: Unit tests for context synthesis and redaction rules
Integration test that fires synthetic alert, verifies PD incident payload and Slack ephemeral view content
Chaos test: simulate downstream tracing API latency and verify enrichment falls back gracefully within 2s timeout
Load test: ensure enricher handles 100 alerts/sec for burst window without increasing alert-to-PD latency above 500ms
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: sensitive data leak via logs or traces. Mitigation: enforce redaction pipeline, require security_review before enabling for services that process PII
Risk: PD rate limits hit with large context payloads. Mitigation: truncate snippets, provide only links plus short summaries
Risk: incorrect runbook suggestion causing confusion. Mitigation: keep suggestion editable and require explicit acceptance to modify incident state
Risk: increased MTTR during rollout due to unfamiliar workflow. Mitigation: provide training docs and opt-in pilot with triage sessions
